SeriesTraverseAccessor API Reference¶

Back to Series API Reference

This is the landing page for the value-driven search workflow entered through Series::traverse. The accessor turns a condition on a Series’ values into the coordinates of every matching position, wrapped in a queryable TraverseMatch.

Why This Family Is Its Own Surface¶

The rest of the Series API answers “reshape / reduce / transform every element.” traverse answers a different question: which elements satisfy a predicate, and where are they. Ordinary comparisons give you a boolean Series of the same shape and stop there; traverse carries the search through to positions, matched values, flat offsets, and a gather helper — one call, one result object.

This is one of the surfaces where Series intentionally diverges from a plain tensor library, so it earns a dedicated reference.

The Calling Model¶

Every finder is available two ways:

// (1) directly on the accessor -- searches the whole Series
auto a = grid.traverse.find_ge(6.0);

// (2) through a proxy that first narrows to a view -- searches only that view
auto b = grid.traverse({std::int64_t{1}}).find_ge(5.0);   // row 1 only

The selector list passed to traverse({ ... }) is the same view-only language as traverse_slice(): scalar indices, positive-step slices, SliceAll(), NewAxis(), Ellipsis(). When you use it, the resulting match’s coordinates and rank() are relative to the sub-view.

Both call styles return a TraverseMatch.

Method Pages¶

Explicit mask¶

  • find_all: match every position where a boolean mask is true (find_if is an identical spelling)

  • find_if: alias of find_all

Value predicates¶

  • find_eq: match positions equal to a scalar or peer Series

  • find_neq: the negation of find_eq

  • find_ge: match positions at or above a threshold

  • find_le: match positions at or below a threshold

  • find_btw: match positions inside a [lo, hi] band, inclusive or exclusive

Mask algebra¶

  • find_and: match where two masks are both true

  • find_or: match where either mask is true

  • find_not: match where a mask is false

Positional¶

  • find_first: keep only the first match globally, or the first match in each lane along an axis, or the first match in each leading batch

Result object¶

  • TraverseMatch: count, coords, values, linear_indices, split_indices, select_from, and the shape/status queries

Choosing A Finder¶

  • Use find_eq / find_ge / find_le / find_btw when the condition is a direct comparison — they build the mask for you.

  • Use find_all when you have already computed a mask, possibly with logic the comparison finders do not cover.

  • Use find_and / find_or / find_not to combine two existing masks without a temporary logical_* call.

  • Use find_first when you only want one representative match per row, per column, or per batch — for example the first crossing of a threshold in each sequence.

  • Reach into TraverseMatch for what to do with the hits: count them, read their values (differentiable), turn them into flat offsets, or gather the same positions from a parallel Series.
